Name: printer_accuracy_hole_shrink_compensation
Comment: FDM holes always print smaller than modeled due to filament expansion and layer resolution. Add to all hole sketch diameters or apply via Offset Face. Measure a 10 mm test circle: shrink = 10.0 − actual_diameter. Update per machine.

Name: printer_accuracy_outer_dimension_oversize
Comment: FDM outer surfaces print 0.05–0.20 mm larger than modeled due to extrusion pressure. Subtract from shaft and boss ODs for precise fits. Measure a 20 mm calibration cube in X and Y.

Name: printer_accuracy_standard_layer_height
Comment: Default layer height. Base unit for teardrop compensation, bridge sag, and fillet minimums. Update when switching profiles — all derived params follow.

Name: printer_accuracy_first_layer_height
Comment: First layer printed thicker for bed adhesion. Relevant for total Z stack height calculations.

Name: printer_accuracy_extrusion_line_width
Comment: Actual deposited extrusion line width — typically nozzle_dia × 1.10–1.15. All wall thickness and bridge span calcs derive from this. Re-measure after any nozzle change.

Name: printer_accuracy_elephant_foot_compensation
Comment: First-layer squish bulge on outer perimeter — typically 0.10–0.20 mm. Subtract from bottom-surface mating features (flanges, bases) so they sit flush. Dial in with a single-layer calibration square.

Name: printer_accuracy_seam_zseam_protrusion
Comment: Small Z-seam protrusion at layer start. Matters on outer mating surfaces. Either orient seam to a non-mating edge, or add this allowance to surface-critical fits.

Name: printer_accuracy_minimum_infill_bridging_width
Comment: Below this pocket width, infill skips entirely and bridges. Account for this in thin pocket features — infill may not fill them at all.

Name: printer_accuracy_solid_top_layers_for_mating_surface
Comment: Number of solid top layers before a press-fit or heat-set mating surface for best dimensional accuracy. Fewer layers = rougher surface = worse fit.

Name: tolerance_standard_fine_iso2768_f
Comment: ISO 2768 fine class (f) — general linear tolerance ±0.05 mm per side for 3–30 mm features. Requires a well-calibrated machine.

Name: tolerance_standard_medium_iso2768_m
Comment: ISO 2768 medium class (m) — ±0.10 mm per side for 3–30 mm. Default starting point for most functional FDM parts.

Name: tolerance_standard_coarse_iso2768_c
Comment: ISO 2768 coarse class (c) — ±0.20 mm per side. For non-critical features or lower-accuracy machines.

Name: tolerance_angular_general_degrees
Comment: General angular tolerance. Matches ISO 2768 medium angular class for 0–10 mm leg length. Critical angles (e.g. 45° for no-support printing) should be exactly constrained.

Name: tolerance_fit_class_fdm_sliding_per_surface
Comment: FDM-practical sliding fit clearance per mating surface (total gap = 0.30 mm). Equivalent to coarse H8/e8 adapted for FDM variation. Use for lids, sliding panels, guide channels.

Name: tolerance_fit_class_fdm_press_per_surface
Comment: FDM light press fit per mating surface (total gap = 0.10 mm). Requires deliberate hand force. Good for retained pins and press-in bushings.

Name: tolerance_fit_class_fdm_interference_per_surface
Comment: FDM interference fit — hole modeled smaller than shaft by this per side. Requires significant force or press. Most reliable with TPU or small features.

Name: tolerance_fit_class_iso_h7_g6_running_clearance
Comment: ISO H7/g6 running clearance fit reference. Only achievable by post-machining or reaming in FDM context. Provided as a design target.

Name: hole_geometry_minimum_printable_diameter
Comment: Minimum FDM hole diameter without post-processing. Smaller holes are often malformed — model at 1.5 mm and drill to final size.

Name: hole_geometry_horizontal_teardrop_z_offset
Comment: Upward Z offset for horizontal holes to compensate overhang droop. Shift hole center up by this, or use teardrop profile.

Name: hole_geometry_fdm_diameter_compensation
Comment: Add to all circle sketch diameters, or Offset Face after modeling. References printer_accuracy_hole_shrink_compensation.

Name: hole_geometry_self_tap_m3_into_plastic_diameter
Comment: Hole diameter for direct M3 screw into plastic (self-tapping, no insert). Use for low-load non-serviceable joints. Engagement length ≥ 8 mm recommended.

Name: hole_geometry_self_tap_m4_into_plastic_diameter
Comment: Hole diameter for direct M4 self-tapping into plastic.

Name: hole_geometry_thread_engagement_minimum_length
Comment: Minimum thread engagement length for reliable printed threads under moderate load. Rule of thumb: 1× bolt diameter minimum, 2× for structural. At M3 that is 3–6 mm.

Comment: M2 bolt clearance through-hole. ISO M2 shank = 2.0 mm + 0.40 mm FDM clearance.

Name: print_in_place_captive_sphere_clearance
Comment: Radial gap between captive sphere and socket for print-in-place FDM. Must exceed layer height to prevent fusion. Tested on 0.20 mm layers — reduce to 0.25 for 0.12 mm layers.

Name: print_in_place_captive_sphere_min_diameter
Comment: Minimum sphere diameter for reliable print-in-place captive joints. Below this the bridge spans become too short for clean FDM.

Name: print_in_place_hinge_pin_clearance
Comment: Radial clearance for print-in-place living hinge pins. Tighter than captive sphere since rotation axis is fixed.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_rotation_angle_deg
Comment: Rotation angle to lock/unlock. Must be less than (360/tab_count - entry_slot_angle) to avoid tab running into next entry slot.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_tab_height_mm
Comment: Radial height of each locking tab (how far it protrudes into the channel). Determines pull-off resistance.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_channel_depth_mm
Comment: Depth of rotation channel in mating part. Tab height + clearance for smooth rotation.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_entry_slot_width_deg
Comment: Angular width of entry slot where tab drops in before rotating to lock. Must be wide enough for easy alignment.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_ramp_angle_deg
Comment: Optional ramp angle at channel end — creates a detent that resists accidental unlocking. 0 = no detent, 5 = light snap, 10 = firm.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_lid_engagement_depth_mm
Comment: How far the lid collar overlaps the container body. Deeper = more stable but harder to print overhangs internally.

Name: twist_lock_bayonet_clearance_radial_mm
Comment: Radial clearance between lid inner wall and container outer wall. Uses sliding fit class.

Name: dovetail_angle_deg
Comment: Dovetail half-angle (from vertical). 60° is standard for FDM — provides retention without excessive overhang. 45° also printable but weaker lock.

Name: dovetail_width_base_mm
Comment: Width at narrow end (base) of dovetail tail. Scale up for larger load-bearing joints.

Name: dovetail_width_top_mm
Comment: Width at wide end (top) of dovetail tail. Difference from base determines lock strength.

Name: dovetail_depth_mm
Comment: Depth of dovetail slot/rail. Deeper = stronger retention but more material.

Name: dovetail_clearance_per_surface_mm
Comment: Per-surface clearance for sliding dovetail fit in FDM. Tighter than general sliding fit because dovetails self-align.

Name: dovetail_slide_entry_chamfer_mm
Comment: Lead-in chamfer at dovetail entry to ease assembly. Applied to both rail and slot.

Name: spring_clip_arm_thickness_mm
Comment: Flexure arm thickness for FDM spring clips (PLA). Thinner = more flex but weaker. 1.6 mm gives ~2 mm deflection before yield at 40 mm arm length.

Name: spring_clip_arm_width_mm
Comment: Width of spring clip arm. Wider = stiffer (scales linearly with width).

Name: spring_clip_deflection_max_mm
Comment: Maximum safe deflection for PLA spring clip arms at 1.6 mm thickness × 40 mm length. Beyond this risks permanent deformation.

Name: spring_clip_hook_depth_mm
Comment: How far the hook protrudes past the mating surface. Must be less than max deflection for the arm to flex over it.

Name: container_wall_thickness_food_safe_mm
Comment: Minimum wall thickness for food-adjacent containers (treats, dry goods). Provides structural rigidity and prevents permeation. Not FDA-rated — for dry pet treats only.

Name: container_base_thickness_mm
Comment: Base/floor thickness for general containers. Thicker than walls because bottom bears load and is the first layer group.

Name: container_corner_radius_min_mm
Comment: Minimum corner radius for rounded-rectangle containers. Smaller radii create stress concentrations and thin-wall issues in FDM.

Name: container_lid_rim_width_mm
Comment: Width of the sealing rim/lip on container lids. Provides contact area for dust seal without excessive material.
